overview.text:
Dwarka, on Gujarat's Arabian Sea coast, is one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage sites; its name is read as 'gateway to heaven'. The five-storey Dwarkadhish Temple, reached by 56 steps from Gomti Ghat where pilgrims bathe first, flies a huge flag with the sun and moon, and offshore excavations have found traces of a city some 4,000 years old.

Beyond the main temple are the Rukmini Temple, Nageshwar Jyotirlinga and Beyt Dwarka island — now reached by Sudarshan Setu, India's longest cable-stayed bridge, opened in February 2024. Shivrajpur, 14.5 km away, is a Blue Flag beach. November to February is the best time; Janmashtami in August–September is the biggest festival.

overview.text:
Ujjain, on the Shipra (Kshipra), is one of Hinduism's great pilgrimage cities and was the capital of ancient Avanti. Its heart is Mahakaleshwar, the only south-facing Jyotirlinga, whose linga is believed to be self-born; the Bhasma Aarti begins every morning at 4. The Mahakal Lok corridor, more than 900 m long beside Rudrasagar Lake, lines the approach with 108 pillars and about 200 statues.

Around the city are the Kal Bhairav temple, where liquor is offered to the deity, the Harsiddhi Shakti Peetha, Sandipani Ashram, Ram Ghat and Jai Singh II's 1725 observatory — fitting for the 'Greenwich of India', on the old prime meridian. The Simhastha Kumbh returns from 27 March to 27 May 2028. Indore airport is 55 km away.
